subject.title: [Bug]: Native Talk button triggers OpenAI Realtime WebRTC call and fails with 500 when Realtime is not configured

question: Should Browser/Control UI Talk require explicit realtime readiness before enabling Start Talk, or should it continue auto-activating OpenAI Realtime whenever usable OpenAI platform auth exists?
rationale: Current source supports both a catalog readiness contract and a recent merged OpenAI auth fallback direction; choosing the user-visible activation rule is product policy, not a safe autonomous repair.

options.title: Require explicit realtime readiness
options.body: Disable or intercept Start Talk unless `talk.catalog.realtime.ready` and a supported browser transport are available, with setup guidance instead of local-TTS assumptions.

options.title: Keep implicit auth activation
options.body: Leave OpenAI Realtime auto-selection from available platform auth in place and only improve the post-failure error text and setup link.

options.title: Add local STT/TTS fallback
options.body: Build a browser/native non-Realtime Talk loop that uses local speech/TTS config when realtime is unavailable, which is broader product work.

recommendation.title: Require explicit realtime readiness
recommendation.body: Disable or intercept Start Talk unless `talk.catalog.realtime.ready` and a supported browser transport are available, with setup guidance instead of local-TTS assumptions.

likelyOwner.reason: The current remaining choice is tightly tied to the OpenAI Realtime OAuth/Codex fallback direction merged in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100671.
